title: Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships and Leadership Programme (Oxford, 2027-28)
organization: Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Trust with the University of Oxford
overview: Scholarship for a one-year master's course at the University of Oxford combined with a year-long Leadership Programme (about 200 hours of training). The Trust describes the Oxford-Weidenfeld and Hoffmann scholarship as fully funded. Application is made through the Oxford graduate application by the course's January (or earlier) deadline.
program_dates: Course of 9-12 months; Leadership Programme from mid-September to early July (2027-28 academic year).
deadline_text: WHT: 'Applications must be submitted by the January deadline to the University of Oxford for the course to be considered... Deadlines vary according to the course.' Reported by secondary sources: 'Deadline: January 6, 2027' (Opportunity Desk); the course's own deadline may be earlier (December).
funding_details: WHT FAQ: 'The Oxford-Weidenfeld and Hoffmann scholarship is fully funded and covers 100% of course fees, a grant for living costs or stipend (of GBP 21,805 in 2026-27) and the full cost of your individual Leadership Programme place.'
Accommodation and expenses for the compulsory introductory days in Oxford are to be covered from the stipend.
The WHT pages read do not mention flights, visa costs or health surcharge.
Partner awards (e.g. WHT-Chevening) may have a different package.
participation_fee: None stated by WHT. Oxford graduate application fee rules were not readable (Oxford page blocked).
stipend: GBP 21,805 for 2026-27 (WHT FAQ); 2027-28 figure not stated on the pages read.
eligibility: Offer of a place on an eligible one-year master's course at the University of Oxford (DPhil not supported)
Ordinarily resident in one of the eligible countries listed on the University of Oxford website
Intend to return to the home country or region to make a difference in the chosen field
Meet Oxford's English language requirement (test must be passed to be accepted onto the Programme)
Select the scholarship in the Oxford application and submit the WHT application form at the same time
nationality_requirements: Ordinary residence in an eligible country on Oxford's list (list not readable this cycle; DRC not confirmed)
education_requirement: Admission to an eligible one-year master's course at Oxford (implies a first degree).
experience_requirement: Not required (WHT FAQ: 'you don't have to have job experience to apply'), but most scholars are early-career professionals with five or more years of experience.
language_requirement: Oxford English language requirement; evidence of proficiency needed.
other_requirements: Commitment to return to home country or region
documents_required: Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Trust application form / scholarship statement submitted with the graduate application
application_process: September: applications open on the University of Oxford website
Submit the graduate application, selecting the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships, by the course's January (or earlier) deadline
Only candidates offered a place are considered
March to June: shortlisted candidates have virtual interviews with the Trust
May: successful applicants informed by the University
eligibility_reason: The bachelor's degree, interests and absence of an age or experience requirement fit. Not confirmed: whether the DRC is on Oxford's eligible-country list (the Oxford page returned HTTP 403), and no English test score is recorded; an Oxford offer is also required first.
potential_issues: Eligible-country list could not be read this cycle (ox.ac.uk returned HTTP 403)
Course-specific deadlines may fall in December
Requires admission to Oxford and an English test
Most scholars have five or more years of work experience, so competition is strong
relevance_reason: A fully funded Oxford master's with leadership training in policy-relevant fields; highly competitive and dependent on an Oxford offer and the country list.

visa.required: Yes (UK student visa for a DRC national); not discussed on the pages read

upfront_cost_risk: Medium: Oxford application fee and English test cost likely; flights and visa not stated as covered.
action: Open the Oxford Weidenfeld-Hoffmann page in a browser to confirm that the DRC is on the eligible-country list and which courses qualify, then check the chosen course's deadline (December or January).
notes: Lead from Opportunity Desk (2026-10-16). Oxford pages blocked automated reading this cycle.

title: Afreximbank Group Internship Programme
overview: Paid in-person internship of three to six months, mostly at Afreximbank headquarters in Cairo (also other Group entities such as FEDA in Kigali). Applications are received throughout the year; cohorts start in January and June. The Bank pays a USD 1,000 monthly stipend, a USD 500 housing allowance for relocating interns, return airfare and a residence visa.
city: Cairo (or another Group entity headquarters, e.g. Kigali)
program_dates: Three to six months; cohorts start in January and June.
deadline_text: 'Open-ended.' 'Applications for internships are received throughout the year.'
funding_details: Monthly tax-free stipend of USD 1,000 and housing allowance of USD 500 for interns relocating from their home countries, paid at the end of each month
Reasonable return fare to the internship location, most economical direct routing from the institution of learning
One week of hotel accommodation (bed and breakfast) during induction; transfer to the hotel on arrival and at departure
Residence visa for the internship, if required
Interns pay their own accommodation (after induction), meals, transport, clothing, medical and group personal accident insurance
stipend: USD 1,000 per month tax-free, plus USD 500 housing allowance for relocating interns
eligibility: Students with proof of enrolment in full-time undergraduate or postgraduate study
Preferred fields include economics, business administration, finance, accounting, social sciences, statistics, law, sciences, engineering
Nationals of Afreximbank Group member states, or students of African descent in the diaspora, or non-African students sharing the Bank's vision
Fluency in English or French and a working knowledge of the other
Aged between 20 and 32 in the year of application
Children of Afreximbank staff are not eligible
nationality_requirements: Nationals of Afreximbank Group member states (the DRC joined in December 2016 according to a news report; the Bank's member list was not read)
age_requirement: 20 to 32 in the year of application
education_requirement: Enrolled in full-time undergraduate or postgraduate study, with proof of enrolment
language_requirement: Fluent English or French and working knowledge of the other; Arabic or Portuguese an advantage
other_requirements: Recommendation from the institution of learning stating the proposed internship period (maximum six months)
Proof of medical and group personal accident insurance before starting
documents_required: Recommendation from the institution of learning
Statement of intent (maximum one A4 page)
application_process: Complete the online internship application form and upload documents
Applications are handled by the Bank's recruitment partner
No response within two weeks means the application was unsuccessful

sources.label: Financial Afrik: L'Afreximbank accueille une nouvelle adhesion (DRC membership, 6 Dec 2016)
Opportunity Desk: Afreximbank Group Internship Programme 2027

eligibility_reason: Nationality (DRC is a member state per a news report), business administration field and English/French fit. The programme asks for proof of current enrolment and a recommendation from the institution of learning; the profile records no current enrolment, and the exact age (20-32 rule) is not recorded.
potential_issues: Requires proof of current full-time enrolment; a 2024 graduate not enrolled may not qualify
Insurance, meals and most accommodation are at the intern's expense
No response within two weeks means rejection
benefits: Rotation across departments of a pan-African development bank
relevance_reason: A paid trade-finance internship that matches business administration and operations interests; access depends on the enrolment requirement.

visa.required: Depends on placement (Egypt or Rwanda); not stated per nationality
visa.support: Residence visa provided by the Bank if required

upfront_cost_risk: Medium: medical and personal accident insurance and first-month living costs must be paid before the stipend arrives at month end.
action: Check whether you can obtain proof of enrolment and an institutional recommendation (for example through a current course); if so, apply on the Afreximbank internship page before the January or June cohort.
notes: Leads from Opportunity Desk (2026-10-13) and Opportunities for Africans (2026-10-12). Aggregators reported a 31 October 2026 deadline; the official page says open-ended.
